title: Deterministic receiver-owned bytecode record slot resolution

features.description: Build deterministic named-record and alias-chain field resolution in lower
acceptance_criteria: Named record TCon receivers resolve to their own lexicographically sorted full field set
Alias chains resolve with a cycle guard while ADTs and unknown names yield no hint
Existing anonymous and row-polymorphic record hint behavior remains green

features.description: Propagate exact receiver field sets through field access, record update, and merged multi-module lowering
acceptance_criteria: FieldAccess carries correct fields for named parameters, call results, function results, and aliases
RecordUpdate carries the base record's complete sorted field set
Imported Motion and Vec3 receivers receive distinct correct hints without changing tuple or ADT lowering

features.description: Delete cross-type compiler scans and enforce exact-hint, by-name read, or loud update failure behavior
acceptance_criteria: No map iteration participates in GET_FIELD index or record-update shape selection
Field access without a hint uses _record_get by name
Record update without a known base shape returns a compile error and cannot corrupt the record

features.description: Add CLI, compiler, golden, multi-module, parity, and repeated-process determinism regression coverage
acceptance_criteria: OOB, in-bounds, record-update, alias-chain, and Motion/Vec3 fixtures match interpreter output in 10 of 10 strict runs
Ten game-shape disassemblies are byte-identical and normal bytecode emits no evaluator fallback warning
Focused compiler and CLI tests, bytecode goldens, make test-core, formatting, lint, and boundaries pass
